sections.heading: One interface for people and agents
sections.body: FrameBridge provides network administration tools and a shared command-line interface for a home Linux network with one human administrator and authorized agents. Desktop access is an auxiliary tool. fb is the short name for framebridge; both run the same program. The tools run on your Linux computers. The ChatGPT model remains hosted. Read this guide for the installed version before operating; confirm the receiver, target and available capabilities. Use the installed CLI and tools for normal work. Edit software only when the owner explicitly requests development, using a separate source clone and reviewable changes rather than rewriting the installed program.

sections.heading: Install and connect
sections.body: Install the package built for your exact Debian 13, Ubuntu 24.04 or Linux Mint 22.x amd64 profile. These are the three release profiles; other distributions and architectures are outside this release. Keep the distribution system Python: 3.13 on Debian 13, 3.12 on Ubuntu 24.04 and Mint 22.x. Use the matching signed APT suite: trixie, noble or mint22. Normal first connection does not require a separate setup, doctor or start sequence. Run connect in a normal interactive terminal; advanced setup is optional for central/node roles and public settings.

sections.heading: Updating and removal
sections.body: Install an official update through the normal package manager when that update has been published. Normal removal stops package-owned managed processes and can retain the user profile and encrypted connection material; it is not a credential-forgetting operation. On systemd 255, package removal also revokes the administrative boot-credential grant. After reinstalling, run fb connect interactively to provision that grant again; retained files alone do not restore startup. Use the explicit credentials forget action first when that is your intended outcome. Do not assume purge erases user-profile data. An explicit downgrade also revokes administrative helper grants before the older package files replace the helper. Helper-backed profiles require a new interactive connect with a compatible package before managed startup can be restored.

sections.heading: Human authentication
sections.body: The normal connection asks for an optional account label, a hidden tunnel ID and a hidden MCP server access key. The label is metadata, not proof of ChatGPT login. Browser login/consent and normal operating-system authentication remain human actions in the normal interface. Never put credentials in chat, command arguments, documentation or example files. A successful managed connection returns to the prompt and can run independently of that terminal. Reboot only when an actual system change requires it.

sections.heading: Choose the right guide
sections.body: Use commands for the reference, connection and lifecycle for state changes, nodes for central/node work, terminals for persistent Bash, and screens for authentic CUA evidence. Query success alone does not mean the connection is ready. The guide describes registered operations; use status/doctor to investigate current state.

sections.heading: Everyday commands
sections.body: connect establishes or resumes the managed ChatGPT connection. disconnect pauses that connection until an explicit connect, including across recovery and reboot. status reports runtime, connection, intended connection state and boot policy. doctor diagnoses prerequisites/problems. setup edits advanced stopped-profile settings. console opens the text work view. help reads this versioned reference.

sections.heading: Services and boot
sections.body: For an already configured managed profile, service start/stop control the current stack symmetrically. Boot enable/disable changes future startup policy without stopping current work or forgetting the saved credential. First node provisioning is an explicit exception described in lifecycle. Without managed setup, non-node service start starts local tools only; normal first connection should use connect. Read status before and after changes. The separate credentials forget action is destructive and requires explicit confirmation.

sections.heading: Console and specialized operations
sections.body: console login manages optional work-view opening after an authenticated tty1 login; it does not enable automatic login. tty service manages the terminal daemon; tty list lists sessions. nodes, certificates and screen-access retain their domain-specific subcommands. Use --help at the relevant command for its exact arguments. Avoid compatibility aliases in new automation.

sections.heading: Human and structured output
sections.body: Use explicit commands in automation rather than the interactive no-argument menu. --json selects structured output for an agent; examine operation success, readiness and state separately. Read errors and the exit status. If human interaction is required, complete it in the normal terminal/interface rather than attempting to supply a secret through the agent. CLI JSON uses an envelope with schema_version, product, version, command, ok and result. Read runtime, connection and boot truth inside result; envelope ok denotes request success. Exit 0 means successful query/operation, not necessarily a connected transport; exit 1 reports operation/diagnostic failure, exit 2 invalid arguments or required human interaction/confirmation, and exit 130 cancellation.

sections.heading: Normal managed connection
sections.body: connect creates the default standalone profile when absent and establishes managed startup. It asks for initial human input in the terminal, checks progress, reports readiness or an actionable failure, and returns to the prompt. Valid saved setup can be resumed without repeating the initial fields. The MCP access key is not an OpenAI API key. Keep the browser's ChatGPT account login and consent separate from the optional local account label.

sections.heading: Saved credentials and next boot
sections.body: Managed startup uses protected, host-bound encrypted connection material. The normal terminal does not have to remain open. This is a persistence feature, not a promise that an account, network or tunnel service can never fail. Connection intent and boot policy are separate: enabled startup runs the stack at boot, while an intentional disconnected state remains disconnected until connect.

sections.heading: Intentional disconnect
sections.body: disconnect keeps local tools and saved material, but records the intention to stay disconnected across worker recovery and reboot. Explicit connect clears that pause. Check the returned state rather than interpreting a successful query as an active transport.

sections.heading: Replacement and temporary foreground mode
sections.body: Use connect --replace only when deliberately replacing the account label/tunnel/access configuration. The advanced --foreground mode is temporary, needs a ready local runtime and occupies its terminal until interrupted; it is not the normal managed workflow. Do not use advanced mode merely to recover a normal saved connection.

lifecycle.title: Services, connection intent and boot policy

sections.heading: Separate states
sections.body: FrameBridge distinguishes actual local runtime, desired connection, verified transport, boot enablement and saved credential presence. A healthy runtime can be intentionally disconnected; a service can be active while disabled for the next boot. Read the labelled status fields together.

sections.heading: Current managed stack
sections.body: For an already configured managed profile, service start and service stop use the same current-stack boundary without changing boot enablement. Stop ends current managed work and transport but keeps profile, boot policy and saved material. Startup on the next boot follows the retained policy and intended connection state. A non-node profile without managed setup starts only local tools. Stopping a terminal service or session can interrupt its running work.

sections.heading: Future boot policy
sections.body: Once managed setup exists, service boot enable/disable changes unit enablement only. It does not immediately stop or start current work and does not delete saved connection material. Initial node provisioning is described separately below. Explicitly forgetting saved material is a separate destructive operation. Legacy autostart disable has its old broader destructive behavior; use the canonical service boot commands for new workflows.

sections.heading: First managed startup for a node
sections.body: After advanced node setup and the required enrollment/approval, a node without a managed installation can run service start in a normal terminal. This first call creates managed startup, enables future boot and starts the node now; the result explicitly reports initial_configuration and boot_policy_changed. Alternatively, first service boot enable prepares and enables the node unit without starting current work. Initial preparation can require normal owner authentication and is not silently performed by an unattended JSON request. Once configured, the ordinary start/stop and boot-policy-only contracts apply. A node does not need its own ChatGPT tunnel.

sections.heading: Console opening
sections.body: Opening console is a view operation, separate from Linux service startup. Optional console login enable/disable changes the owned startup hook after an authenticated tty1 Bash login. This hook does not bypass normal login. Review the command's scope before changing it.

sections.heading: Roles
sections.body: Standalone provides local tools. Central adds the broker for enrolled nodes. A node joins one selected central instance and uses its ChatGPT connection; it does not need another ChatGPT tunnel or phone pairing. Advanced setup selects the role. Preserve explicit authenticated node transport and real identity approval.

sections.heading: Enrollment is not availability
sections.body: Enrollment submission, central approval, node receipt of authorization and a running node agent are separate stages. status reports what it actually knows; an unchecked agent is not evidence that the node is online. Central list/pending/approve and node enroll/poll/status/run have role-specific purposes. poll can complete saved authorization; it is not a purely observational operation. After enrollment, consult the lifecycle topic for first managed node startup and its explicit initial boot-policy effect.

sections.heading: Targets
sections.body: LOCAL means the actual receiving machine. Use enrolled, confirmed aliases or IDs and inspect the selected target before work. Fleet results include requested_target, resolved_target, node_id, hostname and transport from the confirmed descriptor. The compatibility target field can remain LOCAL; resolved_target names the actual local computer. Unknown targets never fall back to LOCAL. Do not guess SSH identities or use historical lab hostnames as defaults. CLI tty --node can use the authenticated node transport. The interactive console command is local; run it at the destination or use an explicitly configured SSH destination.

sections.heading: Transport trust
sections.body: certificates create manages a private central/node transport CA, not a public website certificate or ChatGPT account authentication. Private keys stay protected on the central host; distribute only the required public trust material. Off-loopback broker use requires correctly configured verified TLS. Do not recreate trust merely to work around a connection symptom.

sections.heading: Service and sessions
sections.body: tty service controls the profile's terminal daemon. tty open creates a real Bash session and returns its identifier. Use that identifier for subsequent observations and input. The same Bash preserves directory, variables and work between requests while the session/service remains alive. It does not preserve running processes across an operating-system reboot. Tool jobs use a profile-specific HOME; a job's home directory can therefore differ from the human login home. Commands retain the connecting account's normal operating-system permissions.

sections.heading: Observe, type and keys
sections.body: tty observe returns terminal transcript text, cursor, dimensions and process state; it is not an authentic full-screen image. tty type sends text without automatically adding Enter, though supplied newlines can affect execution. tty key accepts exact uppercase names such as ENTER and CTRL_C. Replace session arguments with an identifier returned by open/list; never guess one.

sections.heading: Lifetime and closing
sections.body: Default real idle expiry is disabled, but a profile can configure a timeout. Global status/list does not refresh each session's per-session activity. close destroys a session rather than merely separating a viewer. Graceful service stop attempts to close its sessions; elevated or unverifiable process state can prevent cleanup. Inspect the outcome instead of assuming that all child processes disappeared.

sections.heading: Sudo mode
sections.body: A session's sudo on/off controls normal privilege eligibility; it does not log in as root or bypass operating-system authentication. Changing the mode recreates Bash, preserving directory and dimensions but not shell variables or internal state. Authentication stays in the normal human terminal/interface. Never send a password through type or chat.

sections.heading: Work console panels
sections.body: console combines an ordinary Bash pane with a read-only FBTERM activity dashboard. The dashboard is not a second interactive shell. The tmux prefix is Ctrl+B: release both keys, then press lowercase z to enlarge/restore a pane, or lowercase o to switch panes. The release accepts common zoom-key variants within its dedicated console. Closing a viewer normally leaves its tmux session alive; leaving Bash, killing its server or rebooting is different. In a desktop terminal the shared work view is horizontal with FBTERM on the left and Bash on the right. Explicit TTY mode is vertical with a short FBTERM monitor above Bash. The layout belongs to the shared tmux window and follows the last requested view mode; it is not isolated per viewer.

sections.heading: Text transcripts and pixels
sections.body: A CLI tty transcript describes a terminal and explicitly does not claim authentic pixels. MCP real-screen CUA-TTY and graphical screen tools operate through the real screen client and capture-linked interaction. Use those supported observation tools when authentic complete screen evidence is required. Never present a reconstructed terminal, animation or partial invented view as a real screenshot.

sections.heading: Automatic graphical discovery
sections.body: The installer and control console stay text interfaces in both TTY and a desktop terminal. Compatible graphical CUA is discovered automatically; availability depends on the actual display/session and permissions. A loaded module is not proof that real pixel capture or input succeeded. New profiles use adaptive auto mode: without a verified active X11 session the runtime provides FBEXEC, FBTERM and CUA-TTY in text mode, without requiring a graphical login or automatically creating a private desktop. Explicit virtual-desktop settings remain advanced options and are labelled separately from physical-screen evidence. Xvfb and Openbox are optional package suggestions and are not installed for the normal connection. Only when you choose a private virtual desktop, install its tools explicitly with sudo apt install xvfb openbox xauth and rerun fb doctor. Installing Openbox can register it as the generic window-manager alternative; use your distribution settings to retain your preferred manager when needed. Physical-screen capture and input currently require the supported active X11 session. Native Wayland control is not validated; showing an XWayland window does not establish full-desktop capture or input.

sections.heading: Guarded X11 text compatibility
sections.body: Graphical TYPE in KEYS mode uses the guarded native X11 backend on x86-64 LP64 systems with libxdo 3.20160805.1. This private candidate accepts active keyboard group 0 only, with no held or latched modifiers and only conventional Caps Lock and Num Lock locked bits. The whole string and generated key actions are checked before any input. Unsupported groups, characters, actions or keyboard states fail closed. The backend does not change the keyboard group or map and does not use the clipboard. Display session, fixed target window, geometry and keyboard context are checked while sending. If input may have started and an error follows, inspect the target and do not automatically replay the text.

sections.heading: Frame-buffer read access
sections.body: screen-access is a narrow, explicit administrative permission for reading the real frame buffer. It does not by itself enable graphical CUA, keyboard/mouse control or arbitrary VT switching. Persistent read access can remain effective after logout or a VT switch; review the command's displayed scope and use normal local administrator authentication.

sections.heading: Shared desktop
sections.body: A graphical desktop shares focus, keyboard and mouse. Use one controlling agent per desktop at a time and avoid overlapping work. This is an operating recommendation, not a claim of certified automatic isolation. Independent non-overlapping execution jobs may be possible; do not infer isolation or physical parallel execution from that alone.

sections.heading: Inspect before acting
sections.body: status summarizes current runtime, connection, desired state and boot policy. A query completing successfully is distinct from the components being ready. Connection verification has a freshness boundary; retrying or unknown must not be treated as connected. Focused status uses the same underlying state model.

sections.heading: Doctor
sections.body: doctor diagnoses prerequisites and reports findings with suggested next steps. It is not an implicit repair, and it is not a substitute for checking actual live connection state. Inspect the diagnosis and relevant private application logs before considering configuration changes. Eligibility checks the exact OS release, amd64 architecture, package profile and CPython ABI before starting native components. The published 0.3.3 scope is Debian 13 with cp313 and Ubuntu 24.04/Mint 22.x with cp312. LMDE 7 and Ubuntu 26.04 builder experiments remain outside that validated scope. A matching profile or a successful development build does not establish a tested installation; never repair an ABI mismatch by replacing system Python or weakening package dependencies.

sections.heading: Local health summary
sections.body: health combines this local profile's existing status and prerequisite observations into an allowlisted report. It identifies LOCAL as this computer and reports the profile, role, connection intent, local tools, boot policy and desktop availability. It never starts, repairs, connects, changes boot policy or creates an absent profile. It does not scan the fleet or probe terminal commands, screen capture or input. States are healthy, paused, degraded, unavailable and unconfigured. An intentional connection pause can be healthy; missing information cannot. JSON result.ok describes observation completeness; result.health.healthy describes health. Health exits 0 for a complete healthy or intentionally paused observation and 1 for degraded, unavailable or unconfigured state. The CLI version is not proof of the running version. Detailed troubleshooting remains local in status and doctor.

sections.heading: Logs and progress
sections.body: Normal connection presents concise progress and a final result, then returns to the prompt. Detailed diagnostics belong in protected application logs. Share only the minimum relevant redacted result; never expose credentials, private keys, browser session data or unrelated personal paths. Avoid rerunning setup, enrollment or broad lifecycle tests merely because a view is confusing.

sections.heading: Authorized scope
sections.body: An agent can use the documented CLI and MCP tools within the user's authorized scope. Reading this guide does not grant permission. Verify the receiver and selected target. Normal human terminal/browser authentication remains separate; do not request credentials in chat or invent phone/Owner-TTY enrollment requirements. Normal use should operate through the installed CLI and tools, not edit or rebuild installed FrameBridge program files. If the owner explicitly requests development, use a separate source clone, make reviewable changes, and do not present a modified build as an official release. This operating guidance does not restrict GNU GPL freedoms or require private forks to submit changes upstream.

sections.heading: Official releases
sections.body: The source is distributed under GNU GPLv3-only terms and the applicable third-party notices. Verify official release checksums and published signatures/repository metadata before installing. Signature verification identifies the publisher and detects alteration; it does not prohibit lawful modified versions. Official releases are reviewed through the project's release process.

sections.heading: Side effects
sections.body: Read status before service stop, credential forgetting, node approval, startup-hook changes or administrative screen permission changes. Explain material scope and consequences and follow the user's authorization. A sensitive operation must report the actual result, not just that a query succeeded. Keep real captures complete and distinguish observations from hypotheses.

sections.heading: Preferred spelling
sections.body: Use the short canonical interface in new documentation and automation. fb and framebridge remain equivalent. Older connect chatgpt, disconnect chatgpt and connection status spellings are compatibility routes. New status scopes replace the need to learn an extra connection noun.

sections.heading: Legacy lifecycle behavior
sections.body: Older root start/stop and autostart commands are retained for compatibility where documented, but their historical scopes can differ from the canonical service controls. In particular, legacy autostart disable removes managed setup and saved encrypted material; it is not an alias for boot-policy-only disable. Read the command's help before using a legacy script.

sections.heading: Versioned help
sections.body: This guide describes the installed product and guide schema. Read the matching release notes for any semantic migration. The CLI help, MCP guide and static web documentation are generated from the same reviewed guide data; a cached manual from an earlier build can describe a different workflow.
